solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Copyist with pen slogs, working to produce holy books

indicators.note: something working is in motion, so these letters are set going into a new order

parts.note: the fodder is copyist plus pen slogs; 'with' is part of the run but supplies no letters

explanation.surface: A scribe toils with his pen to copy out sacred volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges the letters of COPYIST and PEN SLOGS; 'with' only joins them and 'to produce' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, Mark and Luke are grouped as the three Gospels sharing a common view of Christ's life: books of scripture.

clue.text: Provider, one out to be more flexible

indicators.note: 'one out' says the one is taken away, dropped from the provider word

parts.note: a provider is a supplier
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A supplier tries to become more accommodating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes I (one) from SUPPLIER; 'to be' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means bending easily, so the comparative means bendier or more pliant.

clue.text: Piece of material that is smart, concealing the head

indicators.note: the head of the word is hidden away, so its first letter disappears

parts.note: smart, as in sharply dressed, is snappy

explanation.surface: A fabric swatch that looks stylish but hides the top part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing the head' drops the S from SNAPPY; 'that is' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's cloth wrapper, called a diaper in America, is a folded piece of fabric.

clue.text: Rake in hell, heartless type in a spin

indicators.note: the rake sits in the hell word, placed within it

parts.note: the pit is a name for hell
a rake, a dissolute man, is a roue

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: A debauchee in the underworld, a callous character whirling round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'heartless' keeps the outside letters of 'type'; 'in a' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballet dancer's full turn on one foot is a kind of spin.

clue.text: India with little girl seen as a goddess

parts.note: India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a little girl, a younger sister, is sis

explanation.surface: An Indian woman and her young sister are regarded as divine.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian mother deity, wife of Osiris, is a goddess.

clue.text: Dashing youngsters, workers overcome by bitterness

indicators.note: the workers come under, i.e. after, the bitterness word in this down clue

parts.note: gall is bitterness or rancour
worker ants are the usual crossword workers

explanation.surface: Stylish young men and their labourers are embittered.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable young men of spirit and flair were once called by this word, a noun use of gallant.

clue.text: Clue-writers not getting English right? They may be "badgered"

indicators.note: the clue-writers do without these letters, so they are dropped

parts.note: crossword compilers are setters

explanation.surface: Crossword compilers who get their English wrong may find themselves pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not getting' removes E and R from SETTERS. 'Badgered' in quotes means lived in by badgers, not harassed.
explanation.definitionFit: A badger's burrow is called a sett, so these are homes occupied by badgers.

clue.text: Old Conservative involved in clean-up act demonstrates skill in speech

indicators.note: the old Conservative is wrapped up within the clean-up word

parts.note: elution is the washing out of a substance, a cleaning process

explanation.surface: A veteran Tory joins a clean-up campaign and shows off his oratory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' places OC inside ELUTION, a chemist's word for washing out; 'demonstrates' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The art of clear, expressive delivery when talking is speech skill.

clue.text: Wise fool that is not heartless

parts.note: a sap is a fool

indicators.note: a heartless word has lost its middle, so only its outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A wise fool, the paradox, who still has a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' leaves NT from 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapient is a formal synonym for knowing or sagacious.

clue.text: Administrative assistant with style causing harm for one sort of factory

parts.note: a personal assistant is a PA
a perm is a hair style
ill is harm, as in 'wish someone ill'

explanation.surface: An office assistant whose fashion sense does damage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with', 'causing' and 'for' only link the pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant where pulp is made into sheets for writing on is a kind of factory.

clue.text: Fighting unit of soldiers retreating into cover?

indicators.note: the retreating soldiers go into the cover word

parts.note: a top is a cover or lid

indicators.note: retreating soldiers go backwards, so their letters are reversed

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A combat unit of soldiers falling back to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses the soldiers; 'into' puts them inside the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalry or armoured subunit, like a platoon, is a military unit.

clue.text: Plan made by the French youngster, hours having been spent

parts.note: la is French for 'the'

indicators.note: the hours are spent and gone, so they are removed from the youngster word

parts.note: a youth is a youngster

explanation.surface: A French youth's scheme, after hours of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been spent' removes H from YOUTH; 'made by' links.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement or design showing where things go is a plan.

clue.text: She may provide a service, work on one's back?

indicators.note: in an across clue, work on something is placed after it

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: the back of the word one, with the possessive 's, means its final letter

parts.note: to use something is to work it, put it to work

explanation.surface: A racy hint at a woman offering services lying down.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, who works on clients' backs. 'on' places USE after E, the back of 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who gives massages offers, or provides, them to clients.

clue.text: Answers in short red book

indicators.note: the word red is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: Acts is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: Solutions printed in a condensed communist manual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims 'red' to RE; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond to something is to answer it, both verbs in the third person.

clue.text: A sharp sound conveying power, completely shocking

indicators.note: the sharp sound carries the power-and-completely letters within it

parts.note: a ping is a sharp ringing sound
all means completely, as in 'all wrong'

explanation.surface: A shrill noise carrying energy, totally startling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conveying' puts PALL inside PING, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful that horrifies or outrages is shocking.

clue.text: One should know what's in store — as usual first

definitions.text: One should know what's in store

parts.note: stock means usual or standard, as in a stock answer
first is written 1st, with I standing for 1

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper ought to know the inventory, as is customary, before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' links. 1st read as letters gives IST.
explanation.definitionFit: A retailer that carries particular goods should know the shop's inventory.

clue.text: Embarrassed smile when meeting native finally in African country

indicators.note: the smile and the final letter go inside the African country

parts.note: Chad is a landlocked country in central Africa
a grin is a smile

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of native

explanation.surface: A sheepish grin on meeting a local in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives E from 'native'; 'in' puts GRINE inside CHAD; 'when meeting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling mortified or vexed by a humiliation is being embarrassed.

clue.text: Girl of five escaping from cover after papa appears

indicators.note: the cover word comes after the papa letter

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: five escapes from the cover word, so it is removed

parts.note: an envelope covers a letter
V is five in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A girl of five slipping out from under the blanket when her father arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping from' removes V from ENVELOPE; 'after' puts that behind P; 'of' and 'appears' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, borne by the faithful wife of Odysseus, so a girl.

clue.text: Spiced up with vitality, looking hot after gym?

indicators.note: the looking-hot word comes after the gym letters

parts.note: pep is vigour or vitality
PE, physical education, is school gym
a face looking hot is red

explanation.surface: Livened up with energy, flushed after a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Food sprinkled with black seasoning is spiced; figuratively, speech peppered with jokes is enlivened.

clue.text: Part of article, note, that's put up in The Sun?

definitions.text: that's put up in The Sun?

parts.note: a para, paragraph, is part of an article
sol is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A section of a piece in a tabloid newspaper, put up for publication.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the British tabloid; it is just sunshine, against which the answer is raised.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade is opened and held up in bright sunshine.

clue.text: Gasp with a cold, having rolled over in sleep briefly

indicators.note: rolling over turns these letters back to front

parts.note: to pant is to gasp

explanation.surface: Wheezing with a chill, turning over in a doze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having rolled over' reverses PANTAC; 'in' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To doze for a short spell, as cats do in the day, is to nap briefly.

clue.text: Gods had to be captured by writers

indicators.note: the had word is held within the writers word

parts.note: pens are writing implements
had, as in had a meal, means ate

explanation.surface: Deities trapped by authors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be captured by' is the container signal; 'had' means consumed, as in had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman household deities guarding the storeroom were these gods.

clue.text: School subject the girl coming in top loved

parts.note: RE, religious education, is a school subject

indicators.note: the girl comes into the top word

parts.note: a lid is a top
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl who was top of the class in a subject she enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming in' puts the girl inside the top. RE is religious education, a British school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: To have savoured or enjoyed something greatly is near enough to having loved it.

clue.text: During a day our lot toil for little reward

indicators.note: our lot fall during the day, so they sit inside it

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
we means our lot, us

explanation.surface: For a whole day we labour and get little in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During' places our lot inside the day, Saturday abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: To labour hard and long, as in sweatshop work, for poor pay.

clue.text: Catholic in retreat — Paradise he denied, being fearful

indicators.note: a retreating word goes backwards, so these letters are turned round

parts.note: RC is Roman Catholic

indicators.note: he is denied a place, so those letters are removed

parts.note: paradise is heaven
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Catholic on retreat, refused entry to Paradise, is afraid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns RC into CR; 'denied' takes HE from HEAVEN; 'being' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A coward is timid, lacking courage, so this means fearful.

clue.text: Very fit, also absent-minded

parts.note: an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: Someone extremely healthy but forgetful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'also' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacant, unfocused or distracted look is absent-minded.

clue.text: We had reported a garden intruder?

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are taken by their sound

parts.note: we had contracts to we'd

explanation.surface: We had told someone about an intruder in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives the sound of WE'D.
explanation.definitionFit: An unwanted plant invading flower beds is an intruder in the garden.

clue.text: Musical composition charming to listen to

indicators.note: to listen to means as heard, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: sweet is charming

explanation.surface: A piece of music that is delightful to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to listen to' gives the sound of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instrumental movements or dances played in sequence is a musical composition.

clue.text: Maiden possibly meeting horrible thing during dark period

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, so it is an example of an over

indicators.note: horrible suggests the word thing is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A young woman encountering a monster in the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges THING to NIGHT; 'meeting' links. In cricket an over is six balls bowled; a maiden is one with no runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening through the night happens during the hours of darkness.

clue.text: Reeling sensation heightened as LSD diffuses

indicators.note: the drug diffuses, spreading these letters out into a new order

explanation.surface: The dizziness is intensified as the drug spreads through the body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diffuses' rearranges HEIGHTENED AS LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: Dizziness or giddiness, feeling faint and unsteady, is a reeling sensation.
